content: Undang-undang pajak yang baru mulai
berlaku bulan ini, sehingga perusahaan
harus mengubah cara menghitung gaji.
= The new tax law comes into force this
month, so companies must change the
way they work out wages.
undang-undang is not laws in the plural.
It is the law: one act, doubled inside its
own name. There is no single undang
waiting behind it to be found.
undang-undang  an act, a statute
kanak-kanak    a small child
terus-menerus  without a break
tiba-tiba      suddenly
sehari-hari    everyday, day to day
Here the doubling is part of the word, and
an affix goes on top of the pair as though
the whole thing were a single root.
kanak-kanak      a small child
kekanak-kanakan  childish, said of a
grown person
ke-...-an has wrapped the doubled word
entire. sehari-hari is built the same way:
se- and hari, doubled, and left so.
That is the last of the doubling. You now
have all three kinds: the plural of Lesson
13, the manner word of Lessons 31 and 42,
and this one - the word that was born
doubled and can never be halved.
Nenek mewariskan Alkitab tua yang tebal
itu kepada cucu perempuannya, karena
hanya dia yang masih rajin membacanya.
= Grandmother passed that thick old
Bible down to her granddaughter, the
only one who still reads it.
Alkitab takes a capital: holy books are
names. So does God.
Tuhan   God, the one God. PUEBI treats
it as a name: always a capital.
dewa    a god of a religion with many;
Dewata, the gods together.
Core taught you Tuhan and Pareto 1 dewa.
For a god among many, say dewa, never
seorang tuhan.
The capital runs through the whole
subject. Religions, holy books, months
and feasts are names.
Islam    Kristen   Katolik         Press 1
Ramadan  Lebaran   Natal           Press 2
The ordinary words around them are not.
doa     a prayer
salat   the five daily prayers
amin    said at the end of a prayer
berkah  a grace that makes things go
well
kurban  the animal given at the feast
salat is the KBBI spelling; the notice on
the wall is likelier to say sholat.
Para murid mengamati perilaku hewan di
kebun binatang agar mereka dapat
menulis laporan pengamatan.
= The pupils watched the animals'
behaviour at the zoo so that they
could write an observation report.
Lesson 18 put peN- on a verb and got the
one who does it: menulis, penulis.
Put the same prefix on an adjective and
you get the one who is always like that.
Not angry this morning: angry as a
standing fact about the man.
malu   ashamed  pemalu   shy by nature
marah  angry    pemarah  short-tempered
takut  afraid   penakut  a timid soul
The rest of the family, and few of them
are kind:
berani  brave   pemberani  a brave one
kecut   sour    pengecut   a coward
bohong  a lie   pembohong  a liar
tipu    a trick penipu     a swindler
perilaku itself is built the other way:
peri- and laku, the way a thing behaves.
It is the neutral, technical word - the
behaviour of people, of animals, of a
market - where kelakuan carries judgement
and ulah blames somebody outright.
Sepupu saya penakut.               Press 1
= My cousin is a timid one.
